ABOUT — VARIENT DESIGNS

Two crafts, one discipline.

Six years moving between screens and shelves — treating both as the same design problem.

Trained at the MIT Institute of Design, I've spent six years working across two disciplines most studios keep separate — digital product design (research, wireframes, working prototypes) and physical brand design (packaging, labels, identity systems).

Varient Designs is where that overlap lives: interfaces considered like packaging, and packaging structured like an interface. Every project runs through the same process — understand the user, build the system, ship the artifact.

Bachelor of Design in UX — MIT Institute of Design, 2024.

Nutripleks
Biotech

Plant Growth Regulators
& Biostimulants — Full
Packaging System

The existing range had no coherent visual system — inconsistent colour, typography and layout across products, so nothing read as a "Nutripleks" item at a glance. Varient Designs rebuilt the packaging and label system end-to-end, then produced high-fidelity 3D mockups to check shelf impact before production.

The Problem — Identity Crisis on the Shelf

Zero shelf presence, no brand system.

The old packaging was muted, generic and inconsistent — no shared colour scheme, typography or layout across the range, so nothing read as a "Nutripleks" product at a glance. It wasn't just dated; it was actively costing the brand shelf recognition and market share.

Before & After

Same product line, rebuilt from zero.

Beyond Bottles

Cartons, micronutrient boxes & a spreader-sticker bottle.

The system extended past the core bottle line into 100g micronutrient cartons (Ferrous, Zinc, Boron, Combi Plus) and a standalone "Chipkoo" sticker/spreader product — each carrying the same typographic and colour logic so the whole shelf reads as one brand.
